subject: Request: audit coverage + hosting region / bridge letter for EU tenancy
messages:
From: Elena Popov <e.popov@datatrust.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@datatrust.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 12:15:00 +0000
Subject: SOC 2 / hosting + bridge letter question (EU production)

Hi Naomi,

Hope you’re well. We’re evaluating Redwood for a pilot and our security team needs two things before we can proceed to a security review:

1) A redacted SOC 2 Type II report (or an access path to a secure portal) covering the most recent audit period; and
2) If the report’s audit period ends before our expected go‑live (Jul 2026), a bridge letter or interim attestation that covers controls in the gap.

A few clarifying questions specifically for EU production:
- For a hosted (SaaS) deployment, can you confirm whether tenant data can be pinned to an EU region (we prefer eu‑west‑1) and that backups are resident in the EU?
- Does your SOC 2 scope explicitly include data processing, encryption at rest, key management, and personnel access controls?
- For cross‑border transfer, do you rely on SCCs, or do you have alternative transfer mechanisms?

I’ve attached our CAIQ extract to show the items we’ll be validating. Please let me know timing and what you can provide. Our legal team is cc’d for any DPA/SCC redlines.

Thanks,
Elena
Security Operations
DataTrust Solutions
[Attachment: DAT-CAIQ-v1.2.xlsx]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Popov <e.popov@datatrust.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / hosting + bridge letter question (EU production)

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail and the CAIQ.

Looping in Rishi (security/compliance lead for hosted) and Karthik (product ops) to pull the appropriate artifacts and confirm hosting/residency behavior.

Quick answers while we pull the documents:
- We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II; I’ll confirm the exact audit window.
- We can provide a bridge letter template if there is an audit gap.
- We do offer EU tenancy options for customers; I’ll get a short note on default region behavior for hosted vs. dedicated/private.

Can you confirm whether the requirement is strict EU residence for all production backups and logs, or if SCCs + contractual DPA is sufficient? That will help us recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

I’ll follow up with the artifacts within 48 hours.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Elena Popov <e.popov@datatrust.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / hosting + bridge letter question (EU production)

Elena / Naomi — thanks for flagging. Attaching what we can share immediately.

Summary (high level):
- SOC 2 Type II: we performed a Type II covering 2024 calendar year (2024‑01‑01 to 2024‑12‑31). The auditor provides a redacted PDF for external sharing — attached as "Redacted_Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20240101-20241231.pdf". If you need portal access for full report review under an NDA, we can arrange it with our auditor.
- Bridge letter: we maintain an interim bridge letter for customers whose go‑live falls between audit periods; attached is our standard EU hosting bridge letter template "Redwood_EU_hosting_bridge_letter_template.docx". We can customize the wording for DataTrust legal if desired.
- Hosting / residency: for Hosted API customers we provide regional tenancy options; we will by default place EU customers into an EU tenancy (primary region eu‑west‑1) when requested in the onboarding form. Backups and snapshots for EU‑pinned tenants are configured to remain in the EU by default.
  - Dedicated & Private options provide stronger guarantees (single‑tenant hardware and customer‑managed VPC options) if your policy requires physical isolation or air‑gapped architectures.
- Cross‑border transfers: our standard mechanism for hosted EU tenancy is contractual (DPA + SCCs) and technical (AES‑256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, tenant key separation). Keys are managed by our KMS with role‑based access and HSM backing for customers on Dedicated/Private. We can provide key‑rotation and access log evidence on request.
- SOC 2 scope: the report includes control categories around logical access, change management, encryption, incident response, and vendor management. If you need explicit control IDs for mapping to your CAIQ, we’ll provide a control mapping spreadsheet.

Next steps we propose:
1) We attach the redacted SOC 2 and the bridge letter template for your legal/security review.
2) Please confirm whether SCCs + DPA is acceptable or whether you require EU‑only physical residency for all artifacts (including backups and logs). If EU‑only is required, we’ll propose Dedicated or Private and share timelines/cost impact.
3) If you want additional audit evidence (personnel access logs, specific key custody evidence), list the items and we’ll route to our compliance team for a documented response (may require an NDA).

Attachments: Redacted_Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20240101-20241231.pdf (redacted), Redwood_EU_hosting_bridge_letter_template.docx

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redacted_Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20240101-20241231.pdf]
[Attachment: Redwood_EU_hosting_bridge_letter_template.docx]

From: Elena Popov <e.popov@datatrust.com>

Cc: legal@datatrust.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 18:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / hosting + bridge letter question (EU production)

Rishi / Naomi — thank you, that helps a lot. We’ve received the redacted SOC 2 and the bridge template. A couple of follow ups from security/legal:

- Please confirm in writing that the SOC 2 report covers the specific controls: encryption at rest (AES‑256), KMS access separation, personnel privileged access logging, and periodic vulnerability scanning. If you can point to the control IDs in the report or provide a short control mapping that would be ideal.
- Can you provide a short statement in the bridge letter that backups/snapshots for an EU‑pinned hosted tenant will be retained within the EU and not replicated outside EU regions? We can then route the bridge letter to our privacy counsel for redlines.
- For SCCs / DPA: please send the current DPA link (we saw a Drive link in your reply — can you confirm version and effective date) and confirm whether you support SCCs v2 or the EU‑UK international data transfer mechanisms.

If you can get the above as answers or redlined text in the bridge letter by Monday we’ll aim to finish our security review that week.

Thanks again — Elena
